programme: HHEX and MECOM jointly specify a VEGF/Angiopoietin-TEK vascular-developmental output — their target sets read directly as this axis: HHEX drives FLT1, KDR, VEGFA, FGF2, ACTA2, NOS2; MECOM drives GATA2, CSF1R, ANGPT1, ANGPT2, TEK, SERPINE1. HHEX and MECOM(EVI1) are classically paired regulators of hemangioblast/hematopoietic-vascular stem specification, and here their target genes converge on the same VEGFR/angiopoietin-TIE2 module rather than looking like an incidental overlap.
role_in_a: In Parkinson's Disease this axis would act on cerebral microvasculature/BBB integrity — reduced nigral perfusion and capillary dysfunction are documented features of PD, and HHEX's own retrieved evidence ties it to PD only via a shared type-2-diabetes GWAS risk locus (PMID 26499758), i.e. a vascular/metabolic comorbidity route rather than a stated brain-vascular mechanism.
role_in_b: In glioblastoma/lower-grade glioma this axis would drive the pathological microvascular proliferation and neovascularization that is the defining histological criterion separating GBM from LGG (WHO grading); MECOM is independently flagged here as a pan-cancer prognostic transcription factor with direct relevance to glioma (PMID 39576394, PMID 34818047).
shared_axis: Both diseases converge on failure or exploitation of brain vascular integrity — degeneration-associated capillary/BBB compromise in PD versus tumor-driven neovascularization in glioma — and HHEX/MECOM control of the same VEGF-ANGPT-TEK output genes is a plausible convergence point even though the pathological direction (loss vs. gain of vascular function) differs between the two.
reasoning: The module is clearly nameable from the target genes and MECOM is independently placed in glioma by two retrieved pan-cancer papers, but nothing retrieved documents HHEX in brain vasculature or PD directly — its only hit is a diabetes-comorbidity GWAS paper — so the PD side of the story rests on general knowledge of PD cerebrovascular/BBB pathology rather than on anything in the record. Recurrence for both factors is moderate (85-91/207, ~41-44%), well below the dominant factor in this set, and HHEX shows zero ReMap-confirmed binding at its listed targets, so the target list itself is inferred rather than directly observed.
support: PMID 39576394 — pan-cancer analysis placing MECOM's prognostic value directly in glioma; PMID 34818047 — MECOM predicted as a master transcription factor from pan-cancer expression data, glioma included; PMID 26499758 — HHEX/T2D GWAS locus shared with Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease risk, a comorbidity link rather than a direct vascular mechanism in PD.
how_to_falsify: Knock down HHEX and MECOM in patient-derived nigral microvascular endothelial cells and in GBM tumor-endothelial cells, then measure FLT1/KDR/VEGFA/ANGPT1/ANGPT2/TEK expression and tube-formation/vessel-mimicry capacity; if neither cell type shows expression or functional dependence on HHEX/MECOM at these loci, or if ChIP-seq shows no direct HHEX/MECOM binding at these promoters in brain-relevant cells (consistent with the 0/25 ReMap-bound targets already seen for HHEX), the account is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (PD network) versus brain (glioma network) — an HHEX/MECOM vascular signal in a blood-derived network more plausibly reflects peripheral/GWAS comorbidity biology than nigral pathology, which weakens the PD-side claim. The 207 comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the denominator is inflated by clinical subgrouping rather than by independent replication. NR4A2 is by far the most recurrent factor in this pair (141/207) but was excluded from this programme because its targets (TH, SLC6A3, DBH, GCH1) mark a separate, PD-restricted dopaminergic-synthesis axis with no plausible glioma role — its dominance should not be read as support for the vascular story. RARA was removed as tissue-generic, which matters because retinoic-acid signaling could otherwise have been mistaken for a shared driver of this same vascular module. PLAGL2, ZGPAT, ZFP90, SOX3, and the discordant TGIF1 carry no relevant literature and are not part of this account.
